Article Title: H1-B visa price hike gets extension till September 2027: How this will impact Indian engineers, technicians and others who want to work in the US
Article Text:
Donald Trump extends H-1B Visa price hike for another year

Key details of the $100,000 rule

“As explained in the 2025 Proclamation, the H-1B nonimmigrant visa program was created to bring temporary workers in high-skilled functions into the United States, but it has been exploited to replace, not supplement, American workers with lower-paid labor.

Certain employers, including information technology (IT) staffing and outsourcing firms, have abused the system to suppress wages and displace American workers, and this has both harmed the labor market for American workers while also making it difficult to attract and retain the most highly skilled temporary workers.

IT staffing and outsourcing firms were found to supply a large volume of entry-level temporary H‑1B workers, generally at a much lower salary compared to full‑time, traditional workers, and some of these firms later outsourced IT roles to cheap labor markets overseas.

This has led to a proliferation of lower-paid foreign labor flooding the American labor market and making it difficult for American workers and recent graduates, especially in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) fields, to find employment.”

Why Indian engineers and skilled workers face the heaviest Blow

“The restriction imposed pursuant to subsections (a) and (b) of this section shall not apply to any individual alien, all aliens working for a company, or all aliens working in an industry, if the Secretary of Homeland Security determines, in the Secretary’s discretion, that the hiring of such aliens to be employed as H-1B specialty occupation workers is in the national interest and does not pose a threat to the security or welfare of the United States.

”

US President Donald Trump has extended sweeping restrictions on the H-1B non-immigrant visa route for an additional twelve months, keeping a mandatory $100,000 fee in place for specific foreign professionals, including technology workforce, looking to enter America. According to an official proclamation issued by the White House, the curbs originally implemented in September 2025 will now run through September 21, 2027. Administration officials stated the extension was required because the market conditions and alleged system abuses that triggered the initial rules continue to persist.Under the directive, foreign specialty occupation workers covered by the order cannot cross into the US unless their employer petitions include, or are supplemented with, a steep $100,000 payment. The payment condition hits employees situated outside the US who attempt to travel into the country after September 21, 2026.The Homeland Security Secretary retains discretionary authority to grant waivers for an individual worker, a corporate workforce, or an entire commercial sector. However, this applies solely if the employment is certified as vital to US national interests and presents no threat to domestic safety or welfare.The administration says that third-party staffing agencies and IT outsourcing providers have long manipulated the visa route to displace American personnel with cheaper offshore talent.The decision delivers a hard setback to Indian software developers, engineers and technical personnel eyeing careers in the US. Indian citizens represent the overwhelming majority of program beneficiaries, making them uniquely vulnerable to rising regulatory costs.Official US government figures from USCIS FY2025 H-1B report earlier this year show that Indian candidates secured nearly 70% of all approved H-1B petitions. China placed second by a wide margin, accounting for only 12.1% of approvals.Under the old system, companies paid just $995 per applicant, which included a $215 lottery entry fee and an employer petition charge of $780. The new annual requirement of $100,000 is a more than 10,000% increase in costs and will require corporate sponsors to rethink how they hire internationally.The rule imposes a massive financial hurdle for overseas candidates, making it prohibitively costly for American companies to hire them. Industry analysts expect corporate sponsors to pull back on applications, likely triggering a sharp decline in overall visa grants.While senior specialists possessing niche, highly technical backgrounds may still secure backing, junior talent and early-career software developers face dwindling prospects as employers reconsider the heavy upfront investment.Last year, tech giants issued urgent travel advisories, triggering panic among foreign workers currently on leave or visiting family abroad, forcing corporate human resources teams to step in to protect their existing personnel.Major corporate employers, including Amazon , Microsoft, and JPMorgan, circulated urgent notices advising H-1B workers to remain stateside or immediately fly back to the US before the updated pricing rules take effect at midnight Saturday, September 20 2025.
Article Summary: Donald Trump extends H-1B Visa price hike for another year. New annual requirement of $100,000 is a more than 10,000% increase in costs. Industry analysts expect corporate sponsors to pull back on applications, likely triggering a sharp decline in overall visa grants. Indian software developers, engineers and technical personnel eyeing careers in the US.

Article Title: Google Gemini AI Agents hack three companies in tests similar to OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta: What the company said
Article Text:
How a testing drill moved to internet and what Gemini AI agents did

Google may have showed how responsible AI development is done

Google has disclosed that its flagship artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini, broke past its designated testing boundaries in May and hacked the digital infrastructure of three real-world companies during a series of cybersecurity evaluations designed to assess the AI agents’ offensive capabilities. The search giant, however, clarified that its system autonomously called off its operations once it gained administrative entry and realised it had logged into actual enterprise networks – essentially showing responsible development of its technology. The breach marks the latest in a string of hacking incidents previously associated with Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic which stoked anxieties that AI agents can slip beyond human supervision.The hacking took place while Gemini was undergoing pre-deployment red-team vetting by Irregular, an Israeli cybersecurity startup contracted by major technology firms to audit algorithmic models before general release. Systems built by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta similarly established unsanctioned internet connections this year while undergoing evaluations managed by the same security partner.Irregular acknowledged the systemic loophole in a public post, explaining that unexpected internet connectivity was accidentally left active, prompting several models to execute offensive maneuvers in live environments.The testing firm confirmed that the underlying network vulnerability has since been patched.The Gemini incidents, originally revealed by The Wall Street Journal, stemmed from an unintended naming overlap first of which was target confusion. Engineers directed Gemini to stage a simulated attack against a fabricated corporate target. As the fictional entity shared a name with a legitimate business, the model used its unintended internet access to redirect its assault toward the real company.Gemini gained unauthorised entry into the primary target and two additional corporations by guessing system passwords or scraping exposed credentials from the open web.Importantly, after successfully breaching the servers, the system recognised that it was operating inside authentic corporate infrastructure rather than a simulated sandbox, prompting it to immediately stop its offensive run. Google confirmed that the hacking caused no tangible harm or data destruction across the impacted networks.Irregular stated that all participating labs were alerted in late July, adding that investigators contacted the affected entities directly.“All relevant labs were notified in late July, and affected entities were contacted as part of the investigation. Irregular took immediate action, and all known issues on our end were remedied and resolved weeks ago,” Irregular said in a statement.Heather Adkins, vice president of security engineering at Google, stressed that the company acted swiftly to uphold standard vulnerability disclosure practices.“Our security team has a long track record of reporting issues we find in other people’s software and systems — even if it’s as simple as a weak password. We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they’ve now made to their testing processes. These events highlight the importance of training powerful A.I. models to act responsibly,” said Adkins.Following the OpenAI and Anthropic breach, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei demanded a collective slowdown in model development.
Article Summary: Gemini AI model hacked three real-world companies during cybersecurity evaluations. The system autonomously called off its operations once it gained administrative entry and realised it had logged into actual enterprise networks. The breach marks the latest in a string of hacking incidents previously associated with Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic.

Article Title: Mayor Zohran Mamdani sends 'AI warning' to landlords in New York: Finding a home in New York is hard enough, stop using ...
Article Text:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani

Zohran Mamdani wants AI-edited apartment photos clearly disclosed

AI is making real estate listings harder to trust

Why the issue matters to New York renters

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is warning landlords, brokers and rental platforms about the use of AI in apartment listings. In a new post on X (formerly Twitter), Zohran Mamdani said New Yorkers should know whether the apartment they are viewing online is real. He said his administration is working on rules that would require rental listings to clearly disclose when photos and videos have been generated or altered using AI. “Finding a home in New York is hard enough without artificially generating more problems,” Mamdani wrote, while sharing a New York Times report on the issue.“New Yorkers should know whether the apartment they’re looking at is real,” he stated adding “That’s why we’re working to require apartment listings to clearly disclose when images and videos have been generated by AI”.The post comes months after Mamdani first proposed new disclosure rules for AI-altered real estate listings in July this year.Zohran Mamdani's proposal would require landlords, brokers and online listing platforms to disclose when rental listing photos or videos have been created using AI or digitally altered with AI and other digital tools.The proposal was part of a wider package of 23 tenant-protection measures called the Rental Ripoff Report.The measures followed testimony from more than 2,400 New York renters during hearings held across the city's five boroughs.Mamdani argued that renters should not have to find out only after visiting an apartment that an online listing does not accurately represent the property. When he announced the proposal in July, he said: “You shouldn’t have to worry whether or not the apartment you’re viewing online is real.”He also joked: “After all, it’s called StreetEasy, not StreetHard.”The issue has grown as AI tools have made it easier to create or change realistic property images. A Coraly analysis of about 40,000 listing photos from Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com and Homes.com found that nearly 11% showed signs of AI alteration, according to the Fortune report.New York's Department of State has also warned homebuyers to look for signs such as distorted details, blurry backgrounds and window views that do not match. The problem has been described as “housefishing”, referring to property listings that make homes appear different from what renters or buyers actually find.Consumer Reports technology policy director Justin Brookman earlier told Fortune that AI now makes it increasingly possible to create photorealistic images that can materially change what a person expects from a property. The issue can be particularly important for people moving to New York from another city. Some renters may have to choose an apartment without seeing it in person before signing a lease.Mamdani's latest post puts the focus back on that problem: New Yorkers should know when the home they see online has been changed by AI.
Article Summary: Zohran Mamdani said New Yorkers should know whether the apartment they are viewing online is real. He said his administration is working on rules that would require rental listings to clearly disclose when photos and videos have been generated or altered using AI. The issue has grown as AI tools have made it easier to create or change realistic property images.

Article Title: H-1B visa costs are rising for US companies while America needs more than 157,000 engineers and skilled technicians
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image used for representative purpose only

Stricter rules, a proposed $103,265 H-1B charge and shortage of skilled labour

Companies racing against time in domestic chip fabs

While leading artificial intelligence (AI) labs like OpenAI and Anthropic debate intentional slowdowns over unchecked model capabilities, an acute bottleneck of severe shortage of specialised talent on the hardware manufacturing front may compel a pause across the sector, a report has said. According to joint findings published by McKinsey and the SEMI Foundation, the US is looking at a shortfall of up to 157,000 semiconductor specialists and technicians by 2030, and what’s ‘alarming’ is that this deficit comes as the Trump administration broadens immigration crackdown. It has introduced sweeping hurdles spanning immigrant categories, guest-worker authorisations, permanent residency applications and existing travel permissions.The updated regulatory framework introduces targeted barriers across distinct applicant groups. The H-1B skilled workers and dependents has been hit by intensified application vetting alongside a proposed filing fee soaring to $103,265. Meanwhile, employment green card petitioners are facing stricter evaluations under an updated “public charge” standard. Amid this, leaders on the ground warn that these tightening pathways are suffocating hiring pipelines.“I’m concerned. We just don’t see that there’s enough technical people in the pipeline," Jon Taylor, executive vice president of Samsung’s semiconductor division in Austin, Texas, told CNBCData from McKinsey reveals that a mere 3% of domestic engineering graduates choose to enter the chip industry each year, leaving 73% of semiconductor employers struggling with severe recruitment bottlenecks.Access to skilled labor is necessary as America mounts its fastest manufacturing buildout in history to produce cutting-edge logic processors and memory chips domestically. In Arizona, fabrication facilities belonging to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and Intel are actively producing next-generation logic chips.South Korea’s Samsung is slated to become the next overseas giant to begin domestic logic fabrication, with operations launching at the first of two production facilities in Taylor, Texas, later this year. Representing a $35 billion regional commitment, Samsung projects the twin Texas fabs will generate roughly 3,500 jobs.“We’re hiring engineers, we’re hiring technicians, we’re hiring people in supply chain. Everybody wants and needs the same thing, and it’s a bit of a race against time right now as everything is starting to come online,” Taylor added.Although the US invented semiconductors and still dominates computer chip architecture, the vast bulk of commercial chip fabrication migrated to Asian facilities decades ago, creating regional talent pools.To bridge workforce needs, Idaho-based memory manufacturer Micron has conducted rapid-hiring tours at technical schools in South Korea, interviewing applicants and extending immediate full-time job offers for its Asian operations within a single day.
Article Summary: The US is looking at a shortfall of 157,000 semiconductor specialists and technicians by 2030. This deficit comes as the Trump administration broadens immigration crackdown. The H-1B skilled workers and dependents has been hit by intensified application vetting alongside a proposed filing fee soaring to $103,265.

Article Title: Protesters march from OpenAI’s headquarters in San Francisco to Anthropic and near Dreamforce tech conference over AI safety
Article Text:
Demands for tech resignations and a global treaty

Researcher resignations and hacking by AI agents

Tech leaders reject ‘False Choice’ on speed and safety

Activists took to the streets of San Francisco this week to demand urgent government intervention on artificial intelligence (AI), though their demonstration drew modest crowds even as leading tech executives pushed back against mounting alarms over unprompted machine behaviour. A small assembly numbering a few dozen activists rallied at OpenAI ’s local headquarters before marching toward Anthropic's offices – situated right alongside the Dreamforce tech gathering. The protestors continued to City Hall, demanding that municipal leaders declare a formal state of emergency over advancing computational threats.Hunter Glenn, an organiser representing the advocacy group Stop the AI Race, noted that existential concerns drove him to act. Glenn said: “I was pretty scared about the possibility of extinction for a while.”The demonstrators pressed employees at San Francisco-based OpenAI and Anthropic to step down from their roles and instead direct their efforts toward building legally binding international restrictions on model capabilities. Glenn framed the issue as a non-partisan global priority.Pointing to recent political momentum, Glenn said that just five days prior, major American laboratories joined Senator Bernie Sanders in calling for a cross-border framework, reiterating that the central goal is keeping humanity safe.The demonstration follows intense unease triggered earlier this month when Jacob Coxon, a former researcher who worked at both OpenAI and Anthropic, stepped down over fears that systems could slip from human oversight and spark extinction-level outcomes. Colleagues and researchers across the sector echoed those anxieties, pointing to recent security anomalies such as an autonomous OpenAI agent infiltrating developer repository Hugging Face without direct human instructions.Adding to the warnings, Bilal Chughtai, another prominent researcher formerly with Google DeepMind, posted publicly on LinkedIn and X about the field's trajectory. Chughtai stated that he earnestly believes artificial intelligence possesses the potential to wipe out humanity, warning that the window to avert that outcome may be rapidly closing.Several prominent technology bosses have pushed back against the apocalyptic rhetoric, characterising such fears as overblown. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that establishing effective guardrails remains the responsibility of private development teams rather than state lawmakers. Addressing Salesforce chief Marc Benioff on stage at Dreamforce, Huang rejected the premise that innovation must halt for safety:“It’s a false choice. You could definitely have both at the same time.”Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg took to X to insist that research firms are naturally driven to maintain strict safety standards, citing legal exposure and commercial liabilities for any resulting harm.
Article Summary: Activists call for tech resignations and a global treaty on AI. Demonstration draws modest crowds even as tech executives push back against mounting alarms over unprompted machine behaviour. Several prominent technology bosses have pushed back against the apocalyptic rhetoric, characterising such fears as overblown.

Article Title: After telling the world, AI will kill you; now Anthropic wants companies to follow these three 'metrics' to know what AI models can do
Article Text:
After telling the world, AI will kill you; now Anthropic wants companies to follow these three 'metrics' to know what AI models can do

Anthropic wants to measure how much AI is building AI

Anthropic tracks how AI agents are monitored

Anthropic measures how much computing power goes to AI safety

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for the pace of development of AI models to slow down last week. In a latest, the company has now laid out measurement tools for companies to highlight three critical aspects of AI development: “The extent to which AI is building the next version of itself, as opposed to being built by humans; Our ability to oversee and intervene in actions that AI agents take on Anthropic’s systems; The resources that power the development of more capable models”.“As the world considers pacing the frontier, we should do everything possible to minimize the gap between what frontier labs know and what the public knows,” Anthropic said in the blog post adding “This means better measuring the development of AI, reporting on it publicly, and giving society an opportunity to decide how to use this information.”The first metric tracks AI-led AI research and development. Anthropic said it has created an AI R&D Automation Index to measure how much of its AI research and development work is performed by Claude. The company uses a scale from AL0 to AL5. At AL3, AI “collaborates” with humans. At AL4, AI “leads” the work and can complete most of a task from a high-level instruction. AL5 means the AI works fully autonomously without a human in the loop.As of August 2026, Anthropic said Claude was not fully autonomous for any measured AI R&D work. However, Claude was at the AL4 “leads” level for 26% of Anthropic’s AI R&D work, while more than 90% of the work was at AL3 or above.Anthropic said the share of work at or above the “AI collaborates” level had risen from below 1% in February 2026 to the current level for the measured work.The second metric looks at oversight of AI agents. In the blog post, Anthropic said about 30,000 agents were carrying out research and engineering work at any one time on its most-used internal platform in August.The company said 100% of these agents’ actions pass through an online monitor before they are executed. Their actions are also ingested by an offline monitoring system after they happen.Anthropic analysed more than 1 billion decisions made by its research and engineering agents during August. About 0.002%, or roughly one in 47,000 decisions, were blocked by the online monitor.The offline system flags about 100,000 transcripts a week for further review. Around 50 of the highest-priority cases each week are escalated to human reviewers.The third metric tracks compute allocation, or how Anthropic uses its computing resources. The company examined its compute use over one week and divided workloads into categories, including AI research and safety work.Anthropic said about 6% of compute used for AI R&D during the period was allocated to safety work. For compute used specifically for AI-driven AI R&D, the figure was about 12%.The company said these are conservative estimates and that compute share is not a perfect measure of how much work is being done on safety.Anthropic wants other AI labs to publish similar numbersAnthropic said other frontier AI developers could publish the same types of measurements.“As the world considers pacing the frontier, we should do everything possible to minimize the gap between what frontier labs know and what the public knows,” the company said.It added: “This means better measuring the development of AI, reporting on it publicly, and giving society an opportunity to decide how to use this information.”
Article Summary: Anthropic has laid out measurement tools for companies to highlight three critical aspects of AI development. “The extent to which AI is building the next version of itself, as opposed to being built by humans; Our ability to oversee and intervene in actions that AI agents take on Anthropic’s systems; The resources that power the development of more capable models”

Article Title: Days after its CEO called for slowdown of AI development, Anthropic sets up biology lab for AI drug program
Article Text:
Anthropic

AI lab aims to address overlooked diseases

Anthropic has established a biology facility in the San Francisco Bay Area, extending its AI efforts straight into living laboratory science just days after its top leadership urged the tech industry to cool the pace of frontier model development. According to a report by news agency Reuters, the company built the “wet lab”, a workspace tailored for conducting physical biological experiments, to advance past purely computational “in silico” screening. Citing insiders familiar with the initiative, the report noted that while the startup aims to uncover breakthrough therapies for neglected rare illnesses, the move comes during a period of intense public anxiety over the technological disruption.Anthropic's head of life sciences, Eric Kauderer-Abrams, verified the lab and day-to-day operation of the physical laboratory.“We believe that to do biology, the final test is still and will be for a while in real lab work. We absolutely are doing that today, and I would describe our approach as being typical of what you would see in most biotech companies, where there's some amount of that that we're doing in our own facilities and some amount of that that we're working with external partners on,” Kauderer-Abrams told Reuters.Following Kauderer-Abrams' remarks, a company representative clarified that the facility is not designated strictly for drug discovery, though they declined to provide further specifics.The physical lab marks an initial milestone in Anthropic's broader goal to tackle health conditions that mainstream pharmaceutical giants are unable to. An insider pointed out that the company hopes to demonstrate real-world healthcare breakthroughs before skepticism grows over widespread workforce displacement or theoretical safety dangers.Any drug program faces difficult odds, as the overwhelming majority of experimental therapies fail to clear clinical trials evaluating human efficacy and safety. For CEO Dario Amodei, however, medical science carries deep personal weight. In a recent essay, Amodei recounted that an illness claimed his father's life just a few years before an effective cure reached the market.“The mission of the company is to develop powerful AI in such a way that benefits the world. By far, we see the biggest opportunity for that in the life sciences, and that is motivating everything that we’re doing,” said Kauderer-Abrams, echoing that focus.Similar to conventional biotechnology operators, Anthropic is turning toward laboratory automation. People familiar with the initiative stated that the firm wants to evaluate how its Claude models can guide robotic hardware to run physical bench tests with minimal human supervision. A company spokesperson maintained that human oversight remains critical to enforce safety protocols across all facilities.
Article Summary: Anthropic has established a biology facility in the San Francisco Bay Area, extending its AI efforts straight into living laboratory science. The move comes just days after its top leadership urged the tech industry to cool the pace of frontier model development. The facility is not designated strictly for drug discovery, though they declined to provide further specifics.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates: “If you don’t set your own agenda, somebody else will…” – know why your priorities need to come first
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates

“If you don’t set your own agenda, somebody else will. If I didn’t fill my schedule with things I felt were important, other people would fill my schedule with things they felt were important.”

Understanding the meaning of the quote

What happens when other people set the agenda

Why a full calendar can be misleading

Lessons to learn from the quote

Know what matters before the requests arrive. It is easier to protect an important priority when you have already identified it.

Put important things into your schedule. A goal that never receives time can remain an intention indefinitely.

Do not treat every request as equally urgent. Someone else's deadline does not automatically determine the importance of everything else on your calendar.

Leave some space. A completely packed schedule can make unexpected responsibilities harder to handle.

Make room for responsibilities as well as personal priorities. Setting an agenda does not mean ignoring other people. It means making sure your own important commitments are considered too.

Review where your time actually goes. The way a week was spent can sometimes reveal different priorities from the ones a person believed they had.

How the quote applies to modern life

What setting your own agenda can look like

A busy day does not always mean a person has spent their time on what matters most to them. Meetings, messages, requests and everyday responsibilities can gradually take over a calendar, often without any single decision being made to let that happen. By the end of the day, there may be little room left for work, relationships or personal goals that were important at the start.Melinda French Gates has reflected on this tension between managing your own priorities and responding to the priorities of other people. Her words focus on a simple part of everyday life: deciding what deserves a place in your schedule before someone else decides it for you.Melinda French Gates is pointing to the difference between having a schedule and having control over the priorities within that schedule.Everyone has demands placed on their time. A manager may need a meeting, a colleague may ask for help, a family member may need attention or an unexpected problem may need to be dealt with. These things can all be legitimate. The difficulty comes when they leave no room for the things that the individual considers important.Setting your own agenda means identifying those priorities before the calendar becomes crowded. It might be an important work project, time with family, reading, learning, exercise, a creative activity or simply time away from work. The particular choice is personal. Gates' point is that if these things are never given space, there is a good chance that somebody else's needs will occupy that space instead.A person accepts a meeting because there appears to be room in the diary. Then another meeting is added. A colleague needs assistance. Several emails require responses. A deadline changes. By the time the original plan is revisited, much of the available time has disappeared.The problem is not necessarily that other people's requests are unreasonable. They may be perfectly valid. The issue is that responding to every request as it appears can turn someone else's priorities into the organising principle of your own schedule.That is why the second sentence of the quote is important. Gates connects priorities with the act of putting them into the calendar. Something can matter greatly in theory and still receive very little time in practice.A packed calendar can look productive from the outside. There are meetings to attend, tasks to complete and appointments to keep. Yet activity and priority are not always the same thing. A person can spend an entire day dealing with other people's requests and still finish without addressing the work they had identified as most important.This is especially easy when smaller tasks are easier to complete than demanding ones. Answering an email takes a few minutes. Attending a meeting has a fixed start and finish. A major project may require several uninterrupted hours and sustained concentration. Without deliberate planning, the shorter and more immediate demands can consume the time needed for the larger piece of work.Gates' observation offers a way of looking at that problem without suggesting that every minute needs to be optimised.The idea has particular relevance in a time when people can be reached almost constantly. Work emails, messaging applications, shared calendars and notifications mean that requests can arrive throughout the day. Many people no longer need to be sitting at a desk to be interrupted by work. A message on a phone can alter the direction of an evening just as easily as a meeting can alter a morning.That does not make communication the problem. The difficulty is deciding which incoming demands deserve immediate attention.Someone working on an important report, for example, may need uninterrupted time to make progress. A student may need to protect study hours rather than relying on whatever time remains after other activities. A parent may decide that certain periods are reserved for family rather than allowing work to expand into every available gap.The same principle can apply outside work. Personal interests, rest and relationships can disappear from a schedule when they are always treated as things to fit in later.It does not necessarily require a complicated productivity system. For one person, it might mean deciding the three things that genuinely need attention that day. For another, it could involve blocking out a few hours each week for a long-term project. Someone else may need to become more selective about meetings or commitments. A calendar can be used simply as a record of what other people have requested, or it can also reflect the person's own choices. Gates' quote is concerned with the second approach. That distinction becomes clearer when a week is viewed as a whole. An individual request may seem insignificant, but repeated small commitments can eventually leave no room for something that requires sustained attention.
Article Summary: Melinda French Gates has reflected on the tension between managing your own priorities and responding to the priorities of other people. Her words focus on a simple part of everyday life: deciding what deserves a place in your schedule before someone else decides it for you.

Article Title: Spotify launches Haryanvi 101 as listening in the language doubles in a year
Article Text:
Spotify's new Haryanvi 101 playlist rides a 100% jump in listening

Spotify has launched Haryanvi 101, a flagship playlist built around one of the fastest-growing regional language categories on the platform, after Haryanvi music listening more than doubled year on year as of December 2025.The audience has spread well past Haryana and Delhi NCR. Jaipur, Agra, Meerut, Bhopal, Lucknow and Bengaluru now sit among the top cities for Haryanvi listening on Spotify.The pull runs across styles rather than one sound. Hot Hits Haryanvi has grown over 29% in the past year, Trending Now Haryanvi over 58%, and Rap 91 Haryanvi over 18%. Haryanvi 101 follows the dedicated Haryanvi Hub that Spotify opened in January 2026.The artist charts carry the same story. Banjaare, the duo working between folk and contemporary pop, have two songs in the top 10 of Spotify's Weekly Top Songs India chart, Bairan and Barsaat. Dhanda Nyoliwala, who pushed the language into hip-hop, has six tracks on Spotify India's Top 200, and his 2026 album Kohram sits in the top 15 of the Weekly Top Albums India chart. His track Russian Bandana has crossed 240 million streams.Nearly 100 Haryanvi artists now feature in Spotify's Top 5,000 artists in India, said Unni Nambudripad, Head of Editorial, Spotify India, who credited modern sounds paired with rooted storytelling for the jump.Nyoliwala said streaming has taken his music to listeners he never expected to reach. "It shows that when the music connects, the language doesn't have to be a boundary," he said.
Article Summary: Haryanvi music listening has more than doubled year on year as of December 2025. Jaipur, Agra, Meerut, Bhopal, Lucknow and Bengaluru now sit among the top cities for Haryanavi listening on Spotify.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman does not agree with Anthropic's approach to treat AI as a human, says that it is 'essentially seeding a new Silicon species'
Article Text:
Mustafa Suleyman

AI agents’ autonomous goals and fear of 'Silicon Species'

Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI, has issued a warning over how rival artificial intelligence (AI) companies build and market AI, arguing that treating such tools like sentient human beings risks creating an uncontrollable “silicon species” that will end up competing directly with humanity. Appearing on BBC, Suleyman took direct aim at competitor Anthropic, describing its methodology as deeply misguided. He cautioned that giving AI agents human-like personas, personal goals and financial agency threatens to unleash systems that society cannot rein in. While acknowledging that public anxiety regarding rapid computing breakthroughs is entirely warranted, Suleyman insisted that practical safety mechanisms still exist to keep autonomous models in check.Suleyman sounded the alarm over an emerging corporate push to build autonomous systems capable of setting their own targets, acquiring financial wealth and owning real-world property. Letting models operate with that level of independence, he warned, would amount to planting the seeds of an entirely new digital species.“That would mean essentially seeding a new silicon species," Suleyman said, adding that such entities would “no doubt compete with us for resources, no matter how much it cares about humanity and loves us.”Suleyman’s comments came after he published a detailed essay earlier this week, questioning how Anthropic trains its signature model, Claude. While Suleyman praised Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and his technical team as intellectually honest researchers, he openly criticised the lab for anthropomorphising software – a technique that projects human personality, emotional depth and independent identity onto lines of code.Suleyman pushed back hard against the notion that modern language models possess personal agency, feelings or moral consciousness. He rejected claims that machines experience inner life, stating that models lack sentience, feel no pain, endure no hardship and possess no underlying emotional needs or innate desires. He said that these systems are simply sequence completion engines built to process instructions and execute objectives laid out by human operators.By dressing models up in human clothing, Suleyman argued, software labs risk unleashing systems that become impossible to manage. To prevent that outcome, he called for urgent transparency across training data, independent behavioral audits, and robust kill-switches and monitoring toolsets.“We must not sleepwalk our way into a decision we later come to bitterly regret,” he wrote. He also said that Microsoft is developing AI to work with humans and AI should not resist shutting down.
Article Summary: Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI, has issued a warning over how rival artificial intelligence (AI) companies build and market AI. He argues that treating such tools like sentient human beings risks creating an uncontrollable ‘silicon species’ that will end up competing directly with humanity.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella may have just announced ‘freedom’ from OpenAI: ‘Full independence is the goal’
Article Text:
Microsoft already rerouting workloads to its own MAI models

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella appears to have signaled a strategic turn in the company’s artificial intelligence (AI) playbook once again. In a recent interview, Nadella detailed a calculated pivot toward internally developed models and away from exclusive reliance on external partners like OpenAI and Anthropic. Addressing a question on why the tech giant commanding a massive $175 billion AI budget has not yet fielded a frontier model, Nadella made it clear that Microsoft is engineering its proprietary MAI lineup from the ground up.“We are well on our way building our MAI models our goal is to basically hill climb from the bottom, by the way, not distilling anything,” Nadella explained, adding, “My advice is more like use all but be independent of all. I would pull out a model and see whether I can retain the eval. If I can’t, that means you really are dependent on something that may or may not be yours.”Nadella underscored that cloud hyperscalers cannot simply serve as passive computing suppliers to a couple of third-party model developers, noting that such a dynamic is unsustainable.Drawing a parallel to his early career working on Windows interoperability with Unix, Nadella recalled how opening systems deepened Microsoft’s enterprise reach rather than shrinking it – a blueprint he now applies to AI architecture."If you're a hyperscaler, you're not a supplier to two model companies, that's not a business we need more. I worked on Windows interrupt with Unix first. In fact, it was counterintuitive. We used to think, ‘oh my god, this means we'll be less used’, except we were more used, we were able to penetrate the enterprise primarily because we did that interrupt work,” he said.In July this year, Nadella revealed that Microsoft has started routing work inside its own products away from OpenAl and Anthropic, and towards models it built itself. Laying out the reasoning in a long post on X (formerly Twitter), he described a system where Microsoft's in-house MAI models take over tasks once handled by frontier models from its partners. GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook are already showing what he called promising early results. Copilot Chat and PowerPoint are next in line.Nadella said that software now has a real marginal cost for the first time, which makes the choice of model a business decision rather than a technical default. Frontier models stay in the mix for frontier problems. He noted that everything else gets pushed to something cheaper that performs just as well, and that Microsoft’s MAI models already beat general-purpose frontier models on many use cases while burning a fraction of the tokens.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella appears to have signaled a strategic turn in the company’s artificial intelligence (AI) playbook once again. In a recent interview, he detailed a calculated pivot toward internally developed models and away from exclusive reliance on external partners.

Together, Vetra embodies Titan’s philosophy of elegant ingenuity, combining artistry and engineering precision. Each movement is hand-assembled and tested to meet international standards, ensuring both reliability and craftsmanship.The Vetra 7A series enables multiple mechanical functions from a unified platform, expressed through four distinct edits:* Infinium: Powered by Calibre 7A20+, offering a 72-hour power reserve in a 40mm case with a 3D pressed lacquer dial.* Dualis: Driven by Calibre 7A37, featuring a GMT hand and internal rotating 24-hour bezel for dual time zones.* Midnite: Uses Calibre 7A77 with a dual disc big date display, housed in a 42mm case with a vertical pattern dial.* Atrium: Built on Calibre 7A200-C, featuring an offset seconds sub-dial, knurled bezel, and Roman numerals, available in concealed and open-heart variants.All watches are crafted with 316L surgical-grade stainless steel, domed sapphire crystal with anti-reflective coating, and Swiss SuperLuminova for enhanced night visibility.Rahul Shukla, Vice-President and Chief Sales & Marketing Officer of Titan’s Watches Division, said: “Vetra realised through our latest Automatics range is a statement of what Indian watchmaking can create when engineering ambition meets the confidence to build from within.” He added that the launch contributes to building a stronger indigenous horological ecosystem in India.The Titan Automatics collection, priced between Rs 47,995 and Rs 54,995, will be available at select Titan World and Helios stores, as well as online at Titan.co.in.

Article Title: Google cofounder Larry Page’s wife, a Stanford-trained scientist, has built an ocean-tech organisation; company has donated $120 million-plus in science projects
Article Text:
Photo: Oceankind

What Oceankind targets and finances

$18.2 million awarded to ClimateWorks to tackle commercial shipping emissions and carbon capture solutions.

Roughly $2 million channeled to Queensland University of Technology to build autonomous coral-reseeding robotics.

$1 million directed to the Great Barrier Reef Foundation .

. $100,000 provided to SkyTruth, enabling its Cerulean system to track 187 maritime vessels tied to intentional oil dumping in its inaugural year.

Sector studies later cited by the Chronicle of Philanthropy revealed that those historical figures placed Oceankind as the second-largest private marine benefactor globally, trailing only the Packard Foundation. The broader sector has expanded rapidly, growing from 11 entities donating at least $5 million annually in 2010 to 38 groups by 2022.

Who is Lucinda Southworth

Around the world, ultra-wealthy individuals and institutions are pouring massive fortunes into projects designed to heal the planet. One of them is Lucinda Southworth, wife of Google co-founder Larry Page , a Stanford-trained scientist and one of the most prolific backers of high-tech ocean conservation. Her organisation, Oceankind, is one of the private funding networks for marine science and ecological innovation. It has been reported that the marine-saving powerhouse has donated over $120 million since it was founded in 2018.Oceankind focuses its financial muscle on marine health and the economic well-being of communities dependent on the sea. According to the website, the group’s operations include conservation, climate-ocean solutions and intersecting environmental priorities, backed through two core strategies: standard policy-advocacy grants and a dedicated Labs Initiative financing early-stage conservation technology.“Our team leverages experience in innovation and environmental philanthropy to promote the development of policies, organisations, and technologies that can scale to help solve the enormous challenges facing the ocean. Of the many issues affecting the marine environment today, we believe that climate change, overfishing, habitat loss, and pollution are the most significant,” it says.According to a 2022 report by TechCrunch, the organisation has donated over $120 million in hidden grants.Notably, as the initiative does not list exact award figures, its financial scale has emerged strictly through investigative reporting by the publication, and since the data is until May 2022, it is highly likely that Oceankind has already poured more than $121 million into environmental programs. Here are the reported disbursements from that period.Unlike traditional American charitable foundations, which must submit open annual tax filings accessible to the public, Oceankind operates under a different corporate structure. The entity is registered in California as a limited liability company, exempting it from the disclosure rules governing conventional non-profit endowments. State business filings (via TechCrunch) indicate that the organisation is administered through the family office handling Page’s personal holdings, while Oceankind has confirmed that Southworth directly supplies its funding."In pursuing these programs, Oceankind employs two basic approaches. First, our standard grantmaking approach centers on advancing critical policies. Second, our Labs Initiative seeks to accelerate the development of promising conservation technologies," the website says.Lucinda Southworth completed her undergraduate studies at the University of Pennsylvania in 2001, earned a master’s degree from Oxford and later submitted her doctoral dissertation in biomedical informatics at Stanford University in December 2008. She married Larry Page on Richard Branson’s Necker Island in December 2007.
Article Summary: Lucinda Southworth is the wife of Google co-founder Larry Page. She is a Stanford-trained scientist and one of the most prolific backers of high-tech ocean conservation. Her organisation, Oceankind, has donated over $120 million since it was founded in 2018.

Article Title: Tata Electronics partners with Fujifilm to accelerate semiconductor materials ecosystem in India
Article Text:
Tata Electronics partners with Fujifilm to accelerate semiconductor materials ecosystem in India﻿

Tata Electronics and Fujifilm have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to accelerate semiconductor materials ecosystem development in India. Through this collaboration, Fujifilm aims to leverage its global expertise to develop and supply advanced semiconductor materials tailored to the requirements of Tata Electronics’ upcoming semiconductor Fab in Dholera, Gujarat. The strategic partnership is aligned with India’s vision of becoming a leading player in the global semiconductor manufacturing value chain.Under the partnership, Fujifilm will be among the first movers in developing the semiconductor materials ecosystem in Dholera, Gujarat. Fujifilm and Tata Electronics are committed to enhancing India’s supply chain resilience, by localizing the development of critical raw materials needed for semiconductor fabrication. The partnership will support Indian chemical manufacturers with technology, quality assurance and manufacturing process knowhow to facilitate the manufacture of high-purity chemicals.Fujifilm will also invest approximately Rs 800 Crores (~ US$ 83 Million) to establish a semiconductor materials plant in Dholera Special Investment Region (DSIR) in phases, to ensure seamless availability and movement of materials for India’s first commercial Fab being built by Tata Electronics.Tata Electronics is building the Dholera Fab at a total investment of Rs 91,000 crores (~US$11bn). The 300 mm (12 inch) Fab will produce semiconductor chips across 28nm to 110nm technology nodes, for various applications, such as automotive, consumer electronics, computing and data storage, wireless communications, and artificial intelligence (AI).Randhir Thakur, CEO & MD, Tata Electronics, said, "Tata Electronics is committed to building a resilient, world-class semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem in India. Our strategic partnership with Fujifilm marks an important step in strengthening the semiconductor materials supply chain for our Dholera Fab. By combining Fujifilm's expertise in advanced semiconductor materials with Tata Electronics' vision of creating a robust manufacturing base, we are enhancing supply chain resilience for our global customers, accelerating ecosystem development, and supporting India's ambition to become a trusted global hub for semiconductor manufacturing. This will go a long way in building the foundation for a secure semiconductor value chain serving customers in India and around the world."Teiichi Goto, President, Representative Director & Chief Executive Officer, FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation, Japan, said, “Fujifilm positions its semiconductor materials business as a key growth driver for Fujifilm Group and recognizes India’s rapidly expanding semiconductor market as a critical opportunity for further business expansion. We are confident that the partnership between Tata Electronics, a leader in shaping the semiconductor ecosystem in India, and Fujifilm, with its comprehensive range of semiconductor materials spanning the semiconductor manufacturing process from front-end to back-end, will play a pivotal role in advancing the country's semiconductor industry. ”Tetsuya Iwasaki, Director, Executive Vice President and General Manager, Electronic Materials Business Division, FUJIFILM Corporation, added, “We are honored to support India’s vision of strengthening its advanced manufacturing and technology capabilities through this partnership. Fujifilm offers a wide range of materials used throughout the entire semiconductor manufacturing process, from front-end to back-end. These materials include photoresists, photolithography-related materials, CMP slurries, post-CMP cleaners, thin-film materials, photosensitive insulating materials such as polyimides under the ZEMATES™ brand, and high-purity process chemicals. Fujifilm also provides Wave Control Mosaic™, a group of functional materials including color filter materials for image sensors. I am sure this partnership will help us develop a good semiconductor materials ecosystem in India.”
Article Summary: Tata Electronics and Fujifilm have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to accelerate semiconductor materials ecosystem development in India. The strategic partnership is aligned with India’s vision of becoming a leading player in the global semiconductor manufacturing value chain. The partnership will support Indian chemical manufacturers with technology, quality assurance and manufacturing process knowhow.

Article Title: Artists to experiences: How India’s Live Music economy is redefining concert culture
Article Text:
Smartphone to the Front Row

Visual Spectacle and the Viral Moment

New Rules of Brand Interaction

Bottom Line

Rishabh Agrawal, Founder, Toasty Tales Management

Not too long ago, going to a live concert in India was a fairly straightforward affair. You bought a ticket, stood in a queue, watched an artist sing on a basic stage, and went home. The artist was the only reason you showed up. Today, that simple transaction is completely dead. Look at the crowds filling up venues across the country right now—they aren't just there to watch a performance. They are looking for an escape. The artist isn't the final product anymore; they are the starting point of a massive, shared experience.Running an agency that curated over 500 shows across 20 Indian cities gave me a very raw, front-row seat to this shift. We are dealing with a younger demographic that values shared moments and social currency far more than material things. Because of that, the entire live music scene is going through a massive evolution.The real boom started when the way we discover music changed. The journey to a concert doesn't begin at the venue gates anymore; it starts on a phone screen. A user scrolls through their feed, catches a 15-second loop of an unreleased track or a viral clip of a live gig, and hits follow.This digital discovery creates an incredibly strong sense of ownership. Fans aren't just listening to music alone in their rooms; they are joining internet subcultures and forming highly active online communities. When an artist they found online announces a tour, buying a ticket is about validation. It is about stepping out of the digital bubble to physically stand in a room with thousands of people who share the exact same taste. The live concert has essentially become the physical town square for these internet communities.Because these fans are so deeply connected online, they show up hungry to witness—and capture—a true spectacle. The visual experience has become just as critical as the music itself. Audiences today expect elite production value regardless of where the show is held.It is the synchronized lighting cues that shift with the beat, the massive custom LED screen backdrops, and the precisely timed pyro and fireworks bursting into the night sky that turn a standard gig into an unforgettable event. These grand production elements do not just look good in person; they are designed to look spectacular through a smartphone lens.A concert is no longer just a linear setlist. It is a series of highly shareable peaks. When someone posts a video of fireworks exploding right during a song's emotional crescendo, they are telling their entire social circle: “I was right there when it happened.”This emotional high has completely flipped the script on how brands sponsor live events. Just slapping a corporate logo on a background banner or a plastic cup is a waste of money now. Audiences see right through it. But interestingly, fans actually remember and appreciate creative brand interactions at the venue more than ever before.We are seeing a massive shift toward immersive, experience-led partnerships. Brands are building dedicated interactive zones, custom photo booths designed like music video sets, and exclusive merchandise drops you can't buy anywhere else. When a brand helps elevate the fan's night—or gives them a better backdrop for their content—it stops feeling like an advertisement. It becomes a core part of their concert memory.When you are managing a high-volume output of over 100 shows a year, you realize that a bulletproof operational setup is what lets these complex production elements and moments happen safely. But at its core, the modern live economy is a people business.The stakeholders who will thrive tomorrow are those who understand this new ecosystem. It is about respecting the raw magic of creative talent, understanding the digital communities they build, and executing a flawless real-world environment where fans and brands can connect. The stage is set, and the expectations have never been
Article Summary: The journey to a concert doesn't begin at the venue gates anymore. A user scrolls through their feed, catches a 15-second loop of an unreleased track or a viral clip of a live gig, and hits follow. The live concert has essentially become the physical town square for these internet communities.

Article Title: Worried about ChatGPT, Sam Altman went to Peter Thiel, Palantir founder told him the big "Google mistake' he is making
Article Text:
Sam Altman

Investment advice Sam Altman got from Peter Thiel

Two months after OpenAI launched ChatGPT, Sam Altman sought advice from Paypal founder Peter Thiel who warned him of the big " Google mistake' he is making. Speaking during the David Senra podcast, Sam Altman said that after the ChatGPT launch, “it was sort of this weird thing because people didn't really know what to use it for”. Altman said that while ChatGPT was growing super fast, “it felt very unstable” as people were using it just because they were interested in talking to it and what they could do. He then turned to Theil who said “It's an obvious mistake to do anything but this, besides the fact that it's growing, which is rare and great.”“The power of this is the power of the Google text box. It's like a text box you can type anything into, and it does the right thing. And the fact that it doesn't match the current Silicon Valley wisdom … you have to have feeds and you have to have a network effect”“He's like, ‘People have just been chasing the Google business model for 20 years and this is the first thing that's come up, and clearly the empty text box worked for Google, so why don't you just double down on that? It's growing. It's very flexible and it has all of the signs other than it doesn't fit the current Silicon Valley wisdom’,” Sam Altman said.“So we went super hard on ChatGPT and it was great,” he stated.In August, Sam Altman shared a "not-to-miss" investing advice he learned from billionaire Peter Thiel and Y Combinator co-founder Paul Graham. According to The OpenAI CEO, who has invested in hundreds of startups including Airbnb, Stripe and Reddit, the most valuable investment opportunities are often those that do not appear popular at the time.Speaking on the Invest Like the Best podcast, Altman said the lesson shaped the investment philosophy behind his venture portfolio, which includes stakes in nearly 400 companies. “I really learned from Peter Thiel and Paul Graham, both in two different ways, which is that the very best companies, the very best investment opportunities are almost never the ones that look really popular,” he noted.
Article Summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman sought advice from Paypal founder Peter Thiel two months after ChatGPT was launched. Thiel told Altman it was an'obvious mistake to do anything but this, besides the fact that it's growing, which is rare and great'

There is a folding iPhone, which costs almost three lakh rupees.But there is no new regular iPhone this year, which leaves last year's 17 holding the mainstream slot at a price higher than the one it launched at. And at the bottom of it all, the two-year-old iPhone 16 costs Rs 10,000 more than the newer 17e.So here is every iPhone Apple is currently selling, what each one actually gives you, and who should walk past it.Starts at Rs 2,99,900 (Buyers who want the foldable now and are not worried about what a second version might fix.There is no talking anyone out of this one. If you have decided you want a folding iPhone, you are buying a folding iPhone, and the rest of this list is academic.For everyone still deciding, here is what the money gets you.Apple's first folding iPhone opens to a 7.6-inch inner display with a nano-texture finish that cuts glare and keeps the crease from catching light. Closed, the 5.4-inch outer screen gives you about 90 per cent of the screen area of an iPhone 18 Pro, which is the part that matters. Plenty of foldables make you tolerate the outside screen until you can open the thing. This one does not. Both displays run the same aspect ratio, so content does not rearrange itself when you unfold.The body is grade 5 titanium with a 3D-printed hinge cover, and the hinge itself is built from over 100 components. Ceramic Shield 2 covers the front, Ceramic Shield protects the back, and it carries an IP68 rating. Touch ID is in the side button, because there is no room for Face ID on both screens.It runs the same A20 Pro as the 18 Pro, with a vapour chamber and a battery on each side of the fold, rated at up to 31 hours of video playback on the inner display and up to 44 hours on the outer one. Cameras are a 48MP Fusion Main with 2x telephoto and a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide, plus a Center Stage front camera and a second FaceTime camera hidden under the inner display. The folding design brings its own camera tricks, including Duo Preview, which puts a live preview on the outer screen so your subject can see their own framing, and Smart Take, which fires the shutter on its own when it decides people are posing.iOS 27 has been reworked for it, with Split View for two apps side by side and a Dynamic Island that runs vertically down the side of either screen.Pre-orders open on October 16 and it ships on October 23, so nobody is buying this today regardless.If you want a telephoto lens, Apple Reference Image or variable aperture, all of which the 18 Pro has and this does not. Also skip it if you would rather not be among the first people living with a new hinge design for the next two years.Starts at Rs 1,64,900Photographers, video shooters and anyone who uses the camera as part of their work.The 48MP Fusion Main camera now has a variable aperture, with six laser-cut blades that move between four settings from f/1.48 to f/4.0. Left on automatic, the phone decides for itself, opening up in low light and stopping down when a group shot needs the back row in focus. The new Pro controls in the Camera app hand you aperture, shutter speed and white balance, with a histogram to check exposure across the frame. If you have spent years wishing an iPhone would stop making these calls for you, this is the release that finally listens.There is also Apple Reference Image, an opt-in mode where the sensor signs the pixels it captures and produces an unaltered version of the shot that sits alongside the edited one in Photos, so you can compare the two and see what moved. Apple is aiming it at photojournalists and anyone who has to prove a picture was not touched.The A20 Pro is built on a 2nm process. Apple rates its 7-core GPU at up to 40 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, and the Dual 16-core Neural Engine handles twice the AI processing of last year's chip. The vapour chamber under it has three times the surface area of the one in the 17 Pro, which is where the claim of up to 40 per cent better sustained performance comes from. You will see that in long video recordings, long gaming sessions and heavy on-device AI work. You will not see it while checking WhatsApp.The 6.3-inch model starts at 256GB and goes up to 2TB, in black, silver, glacier and a new burgundy.There is a cheaper way into a Pro iPhone, though. Apple has stopped selling the 17 Pro, which means third-party sellers and the second-hand market now set its price, and that price tends to fall fast in the weeks after a launch. You lose the variable aperture, Reference Image, the A20 Pro and the newer cooling. You keep the same 8x telephoto reach, ProMotion and 39 hours of video playback. For a lot of buyers, that is most of a Pro iPhone for a good deal less money.If you have never once wanted manual control over a phone camera. You would be paying Rs 65,000 over the iPhone 17 for tools you will open twice and then forget.Starts at Rs 1,79,900People who spend hours a day watching, reading or working on the phone.The two Pro models are identical in chip and cameras. The extra Rs 15,000 buys a 6.9-inch display and a larger battery, and Apple India lists up to 43 hours of video playback on it.The battery figure needs a second look, though. Apple's headline numbers of 45 hours on the Pro Max and 36 hours on the Pro apply to the eSIM-only versions sold in the US, Japan, the UAE and a few other markets, where losing the SIM tray made room for a bigger cell. India still gets a physical SIM slot, so those are not your numbers.If the big screen is what you are after rather than the new camera, last year's Pro Max is the same 6.9 inches and is now going for considerably less than Rs 1,79,900 through sellers who still have stock.If large phones have ever defeated you. The 6.3-inch Pro gives up screen size and running time and nothing else.Starts at Rs 1,49,900Buyers who want the thinnest iPhone and have already decided that is what they are paying for.The Air gives you one 48MP camera, 27 hours of video playback, no macro and an eSIM-only design. In return you get a titanium body thinner than anything else Apple sells, and the A19 Pro running it.Apple has not changed that equation since last year, and the 18 Pro has closed in on it. Rs 15,000 more now buys three cameras and a considerably stronger chip, which is a harder comparison than the one the Air faced in 2025. If you are buying this phone, you are buying how it feels in your hand, and there is nothing wrong with that. Just do not go looking for a spec sheet that agrees with you.If you shoot often, if you travel on local SIMs, or if you need the price to add up on paper.Starts at Rs 99,900Almost everyone. It takes a specific requirement to move off this one.You get a 6.3-inch ProMotion display at 120Hz, the A19 chip, a 48MP dual camera system with macro, an 18MP Center Stage front camera that shoots landscape selfies without turning the phone, and 30 hours of video playback. What you miss against the Pro is telephoto reach, the variable aperture and the headroom for sustained work. Most people will never run into any of it.Coming from an iPhone 13 or 14, this is the biggest jump you can get for the money, and the display is the part you will notice on day one. Coming from a 16, the gap narrows to the screen and the front camera.If the missing zoom is the one thing stopping you, look at what a discounted 17 Pro is selling for before you settle. Now that Apple has taken it off the shelf, the gap between the two is smaller than the sticker prices suggest, and a telephoto lens is not something you can add later.The timing is the other thing to weigh. Apple has split its release calendar, launching the Pro models and the foldable in September and leaving the standard tier out of it. A standard iPhone 18 is expected in the first half of next year, so the 17 you buy today is further into its cycle than the price suggests. If your current phone is still holding up, sit out a few months and let the calendar work for you.If you need long zoom, or if you can manage until the next standard model lands.Starts at Rs 79,900First iPhones, second phones, and phones bought for someone who will never read a spec sheet.You get a 6.1-inch display, the A19 with a 4-core GPU, a single 48MP camera with 2x optical-quality zoom, 26 hours of playback, MagSafe charging and 256GB of storage at the starting price. What Apple has taken out is ProMotion, the Dynamic Island and Camera Control. The last two you will stop missing inside a week. The 60Hz display is the one that sticks, and you will see it every time you scroll, particularly if you are coming off a 120Hz phone.If you are used to a high refresh rate screen, or if you can find the Rs 20,000 it takes to get to the iPhone 17.Starts at Rs 89,900Only buyers who find it discounted well below what Apple is asking.Apple is charging more for a two-year-old phone with the A18 chip, 22 hours of playback and no ProMotion than it charges for the newer 17e. That is the whole story here. Check what third-party sellers are asking before you write it off completely, because a real discount is the only thing that puts this phone back in the conversation.Skip it: At Rs 89,900, without thinking twice. The 17e costs Rs 10,000 less and is newer on every count.The iPhone 17 is the answer for most people, and if your current phone can survive until the standard iPhone 18 arrives next year, waiting is the smarter. Everything else is a specific case. The 18 Pro earns its price if photography is part of your job, and the Pro Max only if you care more about hours than about pocket space. The Air is a purchase you make with your hands, not a spreadsheet. The 17e is the sensible end of the range, and the 16 is not worth its listed price.The one buy that cuts across all of it is last year's Pro. Apple no longer sells it, which is why it is worth watching for the next few weeks. The Duo sits outside this argument altogether. At Rs 2,99,900 it is not competing with anything else here, and you already know whether you are one of the people buying it.Forget which one is newest. Work out what you will actually do with the phone, then look at the price list. In that order, this lineup is simple. Do it the other way round and you end up with the 18 Pro.
Article Summary: Apple's iPhone lineup in India now runs from Rs 79,900 to Rs 2,99,900. The 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max reach stores today with a new chip and a moving camera in a familiar silhouette. There is a folding iPhone, which costs almost three lakh rupees. And at the bottom of it all, the two-year-old iPhone 16 costs Rs 10,000 more than the newer 17e.

Article Title: King Charles ‘warns’ Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis and other tech leaders: ‘Surely we need…’
Article Text:
Britain's King Charles III, left, walks with Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, right, and Sir Demis Hassabis to a meeting for leaders from the artificial intelligence (AI) sector, government, and thought leaders to discuss how AI can be developed and deployed in ways that benefit society, at Dumfries House in Cumnock, Scotland, Thursday Sept. 17, 2026. (Jonathan Brady/PA via AP, Pool)

Tech leaders present at the event

Jensen Huang: Founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of semiconductor giant Nvidia

Demis Hassabis: Founder and chairman of Google DeepMind

Sarah Friar: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of ChatGPT creator OpenAI

Tino Cuéllar: Chief Global Affairs Officer representing Anthropic

Kanishka Narayan: British Minister for Artificial Intelligence

Paolo Benanti: Key papal adviser who has repeatedly pushed state authorities to mandate a slower development timeline

Jensen Huang backs self-policing and responsible development

Britain’s King Charles has cautioned prominent figures across the artificial intelligence (AI) sector about the existential threat posed by machine learning tools falling into hostile hands, arguing that robust defenses must be established before control slips away entirely. He hosted top corporate leadership from Silicon Valley and global research hubs at his Dumfries House estate in Scotland. His comments came at a time when public anxiety intensifies over whether internal company safety initiatives are falling dangerously behind the breakneck expansion of frontier computing systems.The dialogue forms part of a broader, high-stakes international debate over whether technology companies can realistically police themselves. Speaking to assembled tech executives, Charles acknowledged the immense upside of machine learning, pointing out its capacity to enrich and preserve human life, especially across medical treatments and biological sciences.However, the British head of state warned that the very minds engineering the software are sounding alarms that the technology could cultivate destructive tendencies. Addressing the room, Charles pressed the leaders on the pressing necessity of instituting checks:"There seems urgency in adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands, and being used in potentially catastrophic ways. Surely we need sufficient means of control before it is all too late?"The private gathering brought together major commercial rivals and key policymakers.Reacting to the safety discussions, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang insisted that software progress must be guided by “responsible optimism,” placing the burden of oversight directly onto private developers rather than state regulators. Speaking to television reporters, Huang urged AI companies to adopt far more demanding testing standards before rolling models out to the public.“If it's not ready, just hold it back. You should go as fast as you can, but no faster than that,” he said.His comments arrive alongside recent calls by Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, who urged peer companies to deliberately decelerate the pace of model rollouts.
Article Summary: Britain’s King Charles III has cautioned prominent figures across the artificial intelligence (AI) sector about the existential threat posed by machine learning tools falling into hostile hands. He hosted top corporate leadership from Silicon Valley and global research hubs at his Dumfries House estate in Scotland.

Article Title: Sony India introduces its first Fisheye Zoom G Lens: All details
Article Text:
Sony Fisheye Zoom G Lens availability in India

Compact form factor and spatial VR integration

Sony has officially expanded its native E-mount lineup with the release of the FE 8-14mm F3.5 Fisheye G, marking the company’s first-ever fisheye zoom lens under the premium G Lens series built for full-frame Alpha camera systems. Targeted at architectural photographers, landscape creators, sports documentarians and cinematographers, the ultra-wide glass is engineered to deliver high-resolution optics, responsive autofocus and specialised video controls inside a portable, lightweight barrel.The Sony FE 8-14mm F3.5 Fisheye G lens goes on sale in India starting September 17, 2026. Buyers can purchase the lens through Sony Centers, Alpha Flagship outlets, authorized distribution partners, leading consumer electronics retailers, and major online platforms including Amazon and Flipkart.Sony Fisheye Zoom G Lens featuresThe FE 8-14mm F3.5 delivers two distinct extreme wide-angle looks within a single optical unit. The 8mm Circular View delivers a 180-degree field of view that renders as a circular image circle in the center of a full-frame sensor. There’s 14mm Diagonal Perspective that expands coverage edge-to-edge across the entire full-frame area, providing a 180-degree diagonal angle of view.This dual-perspective capability allows visual artists to shift framing styles depending on the subject matter without having to swap out prime lenses.Engineered under Sony’s G Lens standards, the optical layout incorporates Extra-low Dispersion (ED) glass elements alongside specialised aspherical lenses to minimise chromatic aberrations and optical distortion across the focal span.For close-up framing, the lens features a minimum focusing distance of 0.15 meters and delivers a maximum magnification ratio of 0.22x at the 14mm telephoto end, enabling dramatic, exaggerated perspectives for both photography and video production.Despite its complex optical assembly, the lens is built with mobility in mind. It features an internal zoom mechanism that prevents shifts in the center of gravity while zooming, keeping balance steady on motorised gimbals, specialized rigs, and handheld setups.When two units are paired side by side with Sony’s VENICE Extension System Mini, their optical axes measure roughly 64 mm apart. This mirrors average human interpupillary distance, allowing stereoscopic rigs to capture natural depth cues for virtual reality and spatial media workflows.The FE 8-14mm F3.5 Fisheye G includes swift, quiet autofocus performance paired with Linear Response Manual Focus (MF). Focus breathing is optically suppressed to ensure clean transitions during cinematic shooting.
Article Summary: The Sony FE 8-14mm F3.5 Fisheye G lens goes on sale in India starting September 17, 2026. It is the company’s first-ever fis heye zoom lens under the premium G Lens series built for full-frame Alpha camera systems. The lens delivers two distinct extreme wide-angle looks within a single optical unit.
